rationale: PGS005254 is the better-supported match to the target trait aortic stenosis: its trait_reported/trait_efo are directly aortic stenosis and phenotyping_reported is incident aortic stenosis, whereas PGS005255 is labeled as the related quantitative trait “Mean pressure gradient” with a broader/mixed trait_efo (aortic stenosis, aortic measurement). Both are same publication, same method (PRS-CS), same EUR-only dev/eval, same covariates, and same validation size, so the differentiators are endpoint fidelity and available effect-size strength. PGS005254 also shows a stronger HR per SD (1.64 vs 1.53), supporting better PRS signal in otherwise near-identical context.

PGS002727 is from a disease-focused pediatric asthma study and reports a strong PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.57) plus a large, explicitly multi-ancestry evaluation set (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/SAS each 20%), which is supportive of real-world transfer. Although its AUROC/R² shown (0.66/0.04) appear to be full-model (not PRS-only) and covariates are unknown, it still provides direct asthma-specific evidence beyond generic framework metrics. In contrast, PGS002061 comes from a UKB portability framework paper (“Portability of 245 polygenic scores…”) with only a modest partial correlation (partial-r 0.1184) and no effect sizes or PRS-only AUC/R²; despite much larger training N and disclosed basic covariates, the framework archetype and weaker performance signal make it less well-supported for asthma-specific deployment than PGS002727.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB pan-trait snpnet framework paper with identical covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and the same DEV/EVAL ancestry distribution, so the decision rests on endpoint fidelity and PRS-only metrics. PGS001262 uses a straightforward doctor-diagnosed angina phenotype (phenotyping_reported matches the target disease concept) and shows slightly better PRS-only performance (PGS-only AUROC 0.58683; R2 0.01304) than PGS001261 (0.58233; 0.01228), with both R2 values plausibly below the heritability ceiling. PGS001261’s time-to-event (TTE) endpoint is a mild mismatch for a generic angina pectoris target and does not compensate with stronger PRS-only metrics despite larger training N.

Both candidates have strong endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial fibrillation) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC/C-index values are not directly comparable as PRS metrics. PGS005168’s reported performance is especially confounded by explicit clinical risk-calculator packaging (covariates include CHARGE-AF), making its high full-model C-index (0.8718) largely non-informative for standalone PRS quality. PGS005313 uses only basic covariates (age, sex), avoiding that strong leakage signal, and it also shows a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.82 vs PGS005168 HR 1.67), plus a structurally stronger cross-ancestry method (PRS-CSx) with substantially more variants. Given the lack of PRS-only metrics, the cleaner covariate design and stronger effect-size/structural signals favor PGS005313, but confidence is low because both rely on full-model metrics and differ in evaluation ancestry context.

PGS001135 has clearer, PRS-comparable performance evidence for the broad target trait “arthritis”: it reports PGS-only AUROC=0.539 and PGS-only R2=0.00291 (and incremental AUROC), with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array) and a multi-ancestry evaluation set (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS), giving at least some transportability signal. PGS004477 is more endpoint-specific (“M13 Other arthritis”) and uses a genome-wide LDpred2 score with many variants, but it provides no AUROC/R2 at all and only a modest OR=1.20 with unknown covariates, making its standalone PRS strength and comparability much less supported on the visible fields. Despite PGS001135 coming from a pan-trait UKB framework (a negative archetype signal), the absence of comparable metrics and unclear covariate context for PGS004477 leaves PGS001135 better-supported overall.

Both candidates are endpoint-faithful to atrial fibrillation (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model discrimination is not directly comparable. PGS005168’s reported C-index 0.8718 is heavily discounted because covariates include the named clinical risk calculator CHARGE-AF (risk-wrapper packaging), making the full-model metric likely covariate-driven and less informative about standalone PRS quality. PGS002814 uses only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), avoiding that packaging concern, and provides a strong per-SD effect size (OR≈1.94), which is meaningful PRS signal evidence when PRS-only metrics are absent. Although PGS005168 uses a stronger shrinkage method and far more variants, the explicit CHARGE-AF augmentation makes its visible performance evidence less trustworthy for PRS ranking than PGS002814’s cleaner evaluation context.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/efo/phenotyping all ankylosing spondylitis), study archetype (same UKB portability paper), training size (n=391,124), covariates (basic demographics + PCs), and evaluation ancestry mix/validation N (n=18,262). With no PRS-only AUC/R2 for either, the main differentiators are the PRS-comparable metric and structural properties: PGS002089 shows higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0919 vs 0.0797 for PGS001876) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (22,026 vs 85), which is generally a positive signal for capturing polygenic signal when other fields are matched. Therefore PGS002089 is better supported than PGS001876 on the visible evidence.

Both candidates match the target trait and EFO, but PGS000753 is from a disease-focused AAA genetic architecture study (MVP/Mayo) with a clearly stated prevalent AAA endpoint and provides a direct PRS effect size (OR per SD = 1.37, moderate signal) under basic covariates. PGS001784 comes from a global biobank framework paper (a known underperforming archetype when disease-focused alternatives exist) and its headline AUROC=0.868 is a full-model metric with extensive age/interaction covariates; the only PRS-comparable metric is a small covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.0147, which is below the trait heritability ceiling but modest and not clearly superior to the disease-focused evidence. Given the framework penalty and covariate-driven AUROC concern for PGS001784, PGS000753 is the better-supported choice despite lacking explicit PRS-only AUC/R2.

Both candidates have clean endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all asthma) and only basic covariates (no obvious clinical-risk packaging). PGS001782 has a directly PRS-comparable metric: a covariates-regressed-out/PGS-only Nagelkerke R2=0.048844, which is plausible under the asthma liability h2 ceiling (~0.1515) and provides clearer PRS signal than PGS002061’s partial correlation (partial-r=0.1184), which is less directly comparable to PRS R2/AUC. While PGS002061 has larger training (n=391,124) and broader multi-ancestry evaluation, it comes from a UKB portability framework paper and lacks PRS-only AUC/R2, whereas PGS001782 comes from a multi-biobank global analysis and provides a cleaner PRS-only performance readout (even if evaluated only in EUR).

PGS001135 has clearly comparable PRS-only performance reported for arthritis (nos), including PGS-only AUROC=0.539 and PGS-only R2=0.00291 with basic covariates listed; its PRS-only R2 is also plausibly below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.061), making the metric interpretable. In contrast, PGS004547 (M13 Other arthritis) provides no PRS-comparable AUC/R2 at all (only an OR=1.262) and has unknown covariates, plus its endpoint is a narrower ICD10 subgroup rather than generic arthritis. Although PGS004547 has a stronger structural signal (metaPRS-style method and genome-wide variant count), the lack of directly comparable PRS metrics and unclear covariate context makes it less well-supported on the visible fields than PGS001135.

PGS002738 is the better match to the target trait alcohol dependence on endpoint fidelity: both its trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are explicitly Alcohol use disorder and its trait_efo maps directly to alcohol dependence, whereas PGS000202 is trained/reported as Problematic alcohol use with trait_efo alcohol dependence measurement (a more measurement/proxy-like construct despite DSM-5 criteria count wording). Neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so performance can’t be cleanly compared; however PGS002738 provides a stronger discriminative signal via OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96 (substantial stratification) versus PGS000202’s very small ΔR²=0.00456 and small beta. PGS002738 is also supported by a broader development context (MVP + UKB, multi-ancestry GWAS) and larger validation sample (n=7,900 vs n=1,251), while PGS000202’s main advantage is cleaner/basic covariate disclosure and higher variant count, which is secondary here given the weaker endpoint mapping and weaker effect-size evidence.

Both candidates match the target well (trait_efo=atopic eczema; phenotyping_reported=incident atopic dermatitis) and have identical validation ancestry (EUR) and size (n=337,910) with similarly light covariates, so endpoint fidelity and evaluation context do not differentiate. PGS002755 is structurally much stronger for a polygenic disease (PRS-CS genome-wide shrinkage; 1,090,702 variants) versus PGS004587’s sparse 23 genome-wide significant SNP score, and it also shows a slightly stronger reported PRS effect (HR high vs low 1.249 vs 1.153). PGS004587’s multi-cohort training list is noted, but without PRS-comparable AUC/R2 for either model and given the large structural gap, the genome-wide PRS-CS score (PGS002755) is better-supported to transfer and perform well.

Both candidates match the target trait well (AAA; EFO aligned). However, PGS003972 is structurally much stronger for a polygenic disease: genome-wide PRS-CS with ~1.12M variants and developed from a large, disease-focused multi-cohort meta-analysis context (many AAA-relevant cohorts listed), which typically transfers better than a sparse P+T hits-only score. PGS000753 is extremely sparse (29 variants) and, while it reports a moderate PRS effect size (OR=1.37 per SD), it lacks any AUC/R2 and is based on a smaller, older development context. PGS003972’s reported AUROC (0.69) is full-model and covariates are unknown (so it can’t be treated as PRS-only evidence), but given the strong method/coverage advantage and similarly faithful endpoint, it is still the better-supported candidate overall.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity and study context: same reported/phenotyped trait (M13 Other arthritis), same EFO (arthritis), same publication, same EUR-only UKB development (n=174,489) and EUR evaluation (n=56,192), same variant count, and no PRS-comparable AUC/R2 reported for either. With metrics absent, the main differentiator is the available PRS effect size: candidate_a (PGS004547; RFDiseasemetaPRS) reports a stronger OR per SD (1.262) than candidate_b (PGS004477; LDpred2) OR 1.196, indicating moderately better standalone PRS signal in the same validation context. No covariate or packaging differences are visible to offset this, so PGS004547 is better supported.

PGS005252 is the better-supported match to the target trait aortic stenosis: its trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are directly aligned to incident aortic stenosis, whereas PGS005255 is reported as “Mean pressure gradient” with a mixed trait_efo (aortic stenosis, aortic measurement), making endpoint fidelity less clean. Neither candidate provides PRS-only AUC/R2, so performance must lean on effect sizes and design signals; PGS005252 shows a stronger HR per SD (1.92 vs 1.53 for PGS005255), suggesting stronger PRS discrimination. Although PGS005252 reports a high full-model C-index (0.87), it uses many clinical covariates (comorbidities/BMI/smoking/renal failure) so that metric is likely covariate-inflated and not decisive; still, PGS005255 lacks any comparable discrimination metric beyond HR. Both are EUR-only and similar genome-wide shrinkage approaches with similar variant counts, so the decision is driven mainly by cleaner disease labeling plus stronger HR for PGS005252.

Both candidates are endpoint-faithful for atrial fibrillation (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC (0.78 in PGS005313 vs 0.74 in PGS002814) is only weakly informative. PGS005313 has stronger structural and transportability support: a genome-wide cross-ancestry PRS-CSx score with ~1.27M variants and explicitly multi-ancestry GWAS input plus multi-ancestry evaluation, versus PGS002814’s sparse P+T score (4,520 variants) evaluated only in East Asians. With similarly light covariates (age/sex vs age/sex/PCs) and comparable per-SD effect sizes (OR 1.82 vs 1.94), the method/variant-count advantage and broader evaluation context make PGS005313 more likely to transfer well in external benchmarks.

PGS002727 is more endpoint-faithful to the target context via an explicitly defined phenotype ("Pediatric asthma") and comes from a disease-focused pediatric asthma PRS paper, with supportive PRS signal via a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.57). Although it lacks an explicit PRS-only R2/AUC (only full-model AUROC=0.66 is shown), it has very large and multi-ancestry evaluation support (EVAL includes AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/SAS; validation n=391,820), suggesting broader transportability. PGS001782 provides a clean PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 covariates-regressed-out = 0.048844, below the asthma h2_liability ceiling) with basic covariates, but it is from a global biobank framework-style paper and is evaluated only in EUR (n=7,128) with no effect-size evidence, making it less well-supported for robust external transfer than the disease-focused, multi-ancestry-evaluated PGS002727.

Both candidates are near-clone UKB snpnet scores from the same pan-trait framework paper with the same covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and the same DEV/EVAL ancestry distribution, so endpoint fidelity and transportability context are effectively tied. The differentiator is PRS-only performance: PGS001262 has slightly higher PGS-only AUROC (0.58683 vs 0.58108) and PGS-only R2 (0.01304 vs 0.01185), and a slightly higher incremental AUROC (0.0098 vs 0.00783). These PRS-only R2 values are also plausible relative to the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs ~0.009–0.014), so there’s no inflation red flag. PGS001260 has larger training N and more variants, but within this same study/method family those are weaker signals than the directly comparable PRS-only metrics, which favor PGS001262.

Both candidates align well to the target endpoint (trait_efo alcoholic liver cirrhosis; phenotyping_reported is the disease diagnosis in both). PGS004913 is more disease-focused and context-specific (explicitly developed for alcohol-associated cirrhosis among heavy drinkers; cohorts GenomALC/NIAAA) and provides PRS-relevant effect evidence (top vs bottom deciles OR=4.4) plus an R²=0.029 that is plausibly below the liability h2 ceiling. In contrast, PGS000704 comes from a broad UKB biomarker genetics framework and only reports a full-model C-index/AUC=0.711 from a time-to-event model (age as time scale), with no PRS-only AUC/R²; its HR per SD=1.18 suggests relatively weak standalone PRS signal. Despite PGS000704’s much larger training/validation and more complex genome-wide model, the more endpoint-focused evidence and stronger risk stratification signal favor PGS004913.

Both candidates map to the same EFO target (alcoholic liver cirrhosis) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC/C-index is not a clean cross-model discriminator. PGS000704 is structurally a much more complete polygenic model (183,271 variants; snpnet multi-PRS) with basic, clearly stated covariates (age time-scale, sex, batch, PCs) and very large evaluation support (n=135,300) including some non-EUR evaluation, suggesting better capture of distributed genetic signal and more robust estimation. PGS001777 is a very sparse 3-variant score with unknown covariates and a small evaluation sample (n=1,390); despite a strong top-vs-bottom OR, its sparse construction and limited validation context make it less likely to generalize as a standalone PRS for the target trait. Therefore PGS000704 is better-supported on visible fields.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target (same trait_reported, trait_efo, phenotyping_reported, method PRS-CS, EUR-only GWAS/EVAL, same publication), so the decision hinges on the limited performance evidence. PGS000201 shows materially stronger PRS contribution than PGS000202: higher ΔR² vs covariates (0.01192 vs 0.00456) and a larger/surviving effect size (β=0.099, SE=0.01 vs β=0.043, SE=0.019). Although PGS000201 uses a slightly heavier but still basic covariate set (adds array/site), that does not look like clinical leakage and does not explain away the stronger incremental signal. Variant counts are similar and validation N differences are a weak tie-break, so the stronger incremental/effect evidence makes PGS000201 better-supported.

PGS002738 is the better match to the target trait (alcohol dependence) on endpoint fidelity: both its trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are Alcohol use disorder and its trait_efo maps directly to alcohol dependence, whereas PGS000201 is labeled as “Problematic alcohol use” with trait_efo “alcohol dependence measurement,” which is a more measurement/proxy-like construct despite a DSM-5 criteria-count phenotype. Neither candidate reports clean PRS-only AUC/R2, so performance can’t be compared directly; however PGS002738 provides a reasonably strong risk-stratification effect size (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96), while PGS000201 only shows a small incremental ΔR² (0.01192) alongside covariate-adjusted modeling. With similar EUR-only evaluation and similar validation N, the more diagnosis-aligned endpoint plus stronger effect-size signal favors PGS002738.

Both candidates have exact endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all abdominal aortic aneurysm) and EUR-only evaluation. However, PGS001784 comes from a clear portability/framework paper (“Global Biobank analyses… across diverse cohorts”), which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused scores unless it has clearly superior endpoint+metric evidence. Its very high AUROC (0.868) is a full-model metric with explicit covariates (age/sex/PCs), while its PRS-comparable signal is modest (PGS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.0147), and no PGS-only AUROC is provided. PGS003972 is from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet; many AAA-relevant cohorts including MVP/UKB/deCODE/eMERGE), uses a strong genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with higher variant count (~1.12M vs ~0.91M), and avoids the framework penalty; although it lacks PRS-only metrics (only a full-model AUROC 0.69 with unknown covariates), the overall study archetype and construction are more likely to transfer well than the framework-derived score whose apparent AUROC advantage is likely covariate-driven.

Both candidates are endpoint-faithful to aortic stenosis (incident cases), EUR-only development/evaluation, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on effect-size evidence and design cleanliness. PGS005254 has a larger training sample (n=205,483 vs n=47,691) and reports a clear PRS effect size with CI (HR=1.64, 1.50–1.78) under relatively basic covariates (age, age^2, sex, PCs), which is more comparable to standalone PRS performance. PGS005252 reports a higher HR (1.92) but its selected discrimination metric is a full-model C-index=0.87 alongside a much heavier clinical covariate set (multiple comorbidities and BMI/smoking/renal failure), making the visible performance evidence more likely covariate-driven and less comparable; it also lacks CI for the HR. Given the cleaner evaluation context and stronger training support, PGS005254 is better-supported on the visible fields.

PGS004587 is better aligned to the target trait as a general atopic eczema/atopic dermatitis endpoint (phenotyping_reported: incident atopic dermatitis), whereas PGS001773 targets a narrower subtype (moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis), which is a partial endpoint mismatch for generic “atopic eczema”. Neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R2; PGS001773’s very high AUROC=0.93 and R²=0.49 are full-model metrics (not PRS-comparable) and are further confounded by inclusion of parental ethnicity covariates, so they cannot be used as strong evidence of PRS quality and also look implausibly high relative to the eczema heritability ceiling. PGS004587, while sparse (23 GWS SNPs) and reporting only an HR (1.153 high vs low PRS), is evaluated in a large EUR cohort (n=337,910) with relatively standard covariates and has cleaner trait-to-target fidelity than the covariate-inflated, subtype-specific PGS001773.

Both candidates have strong endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match ankylosing spondylitis) and both are UKB-derived framework-style scores, so phenotype alignment and study archetype do not separate them. PGS001267 has clearly reported PRS-comparable performance (PGS-only AUROC=0.7265 and PGS-only R2=0.0988) with only basic covariates, and its PRS-only R2 is plausibly below the provided liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.399), making the metric interpretable. PGS001876 lacks PRS-only AUC/R2 entirely and reports only partial correlation (partial-r=0.0797), which is less directly comparable and provides weaker evidence of standalone PRS discrimination. While PGS001876 has more variants (85 vs 10) and larger training N, those structural signals do not outweigh the much stronger, cleaner PRS-only metric evidence available for PGS001267.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB pan-trait snpnet framework paper with identical training cohort (UKB), training N (269,704), covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), ancestry setup (DEV EUR; EVAL multi-ancestry with selected EUR), and validation N (24,905), so endpoint and transportability evidence are essentially tied. PGS001261 has slightly better PRS-comparable performance (PGS-only AUROC 0.58233 vs 0.58108; PGS-only R2 0.01228 vs 0.01185; incremental AUROC 0.00796 vs 0.00783) and a marginally higher full-model AUROC/R2, while remaining plausible under the heritability ceiling sanity check. The only counterpoint is PGS001261’s time-to-event phenotyping label versus PGS001260’s generic 'Angina', but given the shared EFO mapping and otherwise identical design, the small but consistent metric edge favors PGS001261.

PGS002755 is better supported for the target trait (atopic eczema) because its endpoint is a general atopic dermatitis diagnosis framed as incident disease (phenotyping_reported: "Incident atopic dermatitis"), which aligns well with the broad target concept, whereas PGS001773 targets a narrower subtype ("Moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis"), reducing endpoint fidelity for generic atopic eczema risk. Neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R2, but PGS001773’s very high reported AUROC=0.93 and R²=0.49 are full-model metrics with covariates including parental ethnicity, making them non-comparable and potentially covariate-driven; the R² is also implausibly high relative to the provided eczema heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.07), further discounting it. Structurally, PGS002755 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants and large EUR evaluation (n=337,910) plus a modest HR (1.249 high vs low PRS), which is more consistent with a polygenic architecture than PGS001773’s 25-variant score evaluated in a small sample (n=676).

Both candidates have exact endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all ankylosing spondylitis) and similarly basic covariates (no obvious clinical leakage). However, PGS001267 comes from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”) with an extremely sparse 10-variant snpnet model, which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly despite clean PRS-only AUROC/R2 reporting (PGS-only AUROC 0.7265; R2 0.0988). PGS002089 is also a UKB framework/portability paper, but uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far broader variant coverage (22,026 variants) and includes explicit multi-ancestry evaluation (EUR/GME/SAS), which is more consistent with robust external transfer. Although PGS002089 lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 (only partial-r=0.0919), the structural and transportability signals favor it over the very sparse pan-trait model.

Both candidates align to the target (trait_efo alcoholic liver cirrhosis), but PGS004913 has cleaner endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported matches alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis, whereas PGS001777 lists "Cirrhosis (males)" which is less specific and suggests a sex-restricted phenotype). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC=0.671 in PGS001777 is not a comparable PRS metric; instead, structural/study signals matter more. PGS004913 is a more standard polygenic construction (PRSice-2, 20 variants) with explicit basic covariates (age/sex/PCs) and larger, disease-focused training/validation (training n=3,037; validation n=3,360) versus PGS001777’s very sparse 3-variant score with N/A training size and unknown covariates. Effect-size evidence is broadly similar (OR top-vs-bottom 4.4 for PGS004913 vs 6.18 top20%-vs-bottom20% for PGS001777, not directly comparable), so the better-specified phenotype/covariates and more polygenic construction favor PGS004913.

Both candidates are near-clones: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (basal cell carcinoma), same publication family, same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry, same training cohort (MGI) and sizes, same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC ~0.632, which is not PRS-comparable). With endpoints and evaluation context effectively tied, the only visible differentiator is slightly stronger performance signals for PGS000454: marginally higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0489 vs 0.0487) and higher top-1% vs rest OR (3.79 vs 3.61) while overall per-SD OR is essentially identical. Given the tiny differences and reliance on full-model metrics, confidence is low, but PGS000454 has the slight edge.

PGS002786 has better endpoint fidelity to the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo are bipolar disorder), whereas PGS002788 is explicitly bipolar II disorder (a subtype mismatch for a generic bipolar disorder target). Both are otherwise near-clones: same publication, same method (SDPR), similar variant counts, same EUR-only GWAS/EVAL, same covariates (age, PCs1-3), same validation N (2,524), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2—only small partial R² values that are not clearly PRS-comparable. With metrics and design essentially tied, the broader direct-match phenotype alignment makes PGS002786 the safer pick.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same publication, same method (SDPR), same training cohort (PGC), and same EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only small partial R² values). Endpoint fidelity to the target trait is weak for both because phenotyping_reported is not a bipolar diagnosis endpoint (PGS002786: cognitive function; PGS002787: DSM5 depression behavior). With no clean PRS-only metrics and similar covariates (age, PCs1-3), the only differentiators are minor: PGS002787 has slightly higher reported partial R² (0.00275 vs 0.00251), while PGS002786 has a slightly larger variant count and slightly larger validation N. Given the domain guidance that small full-model/partial-R² differences are weak but still the only performance signal available here, PGS002787 narrowly wins on the (slightly) stronger reported PRS association signal.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity (identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), study archetype (same UKB portability paper), covariates (basic demographics + PCs), training size, and evaluation ancestry/validation N, and they show essentially identical PRS-comparable performance evidence (partial-r 0.0563 for PGS002034 vs 0.0562 for PGS001826; no PRS-only AUC/R2 for either). With metrics and design effectively tied, the structural signal breaks the tie: PGS002034 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (32,552 vs 45), which is generally more likely to capture polygenic signal than an extremely sparse penalized-regression score in this framework setting. The advantage is modest given the near-identical observed partial-r, hence moderate confidence.

PGS001033 has the closest endpoint alignment to the target: trait_efo is exactly "blood coagulation disease" and phenotyping_reported is a coagulation-defects diagnosis (albeit time-to-event). It also provides clean PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.634 and PGS-only R²=0.0578) with only basic covariates, plus broader evaluation ancestry coverage (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS). In contrast, PGS001826 targets a much narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency subtype (vitamin K–dependent factor deficiency) rather than the broad blood coagulation disease concept, and it lacks PRS-only AUROC/R² (only a small partial correlation is reported), making its predictive support weaker and less comparable despite a larger training N and more variants.

Both candidates are near-clones: same trait/phenotyping (basal cell carcinoma), same publication and release date, same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry, same training cohort (MGI) and sizes, and same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so only full-model metrics and effect sizes can weakly differentiate. PGS000452 has slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.632 vs 0.630) and higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0487 vs 0.0456), while PGS000456 has a slightly higher top-1% vs rest OR (3.95 vs 3.61). Given the minimal differences and identical design, the small edge in overall discrimination/R² favors PGS000452, but the decision is low-confidence because the metrics are full-model and differences are tiny.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), study archetype (same UKB portability paper), covariates (basic demographics + PCs), training size, ancestry distribution, and they report essentially identical PRS-comparable performance evidence (partial-r=0.0716 with overlapping CIs; no PRS-only AUC/R2 for either). With metrics and design not differentiating, the main remaining structural signal is model construction: PGS002032 uses genome-wide shrinkage (LDpred2) with far broader variant coverage (19,768 variants) versus PGS001824’s very sparse penalized regression score (22 variants). Given equal observed partial-r, the broader-coverage LDpred2 score is more likely to be robust/transferable than an ultra-sparse 22-variant model, so PGS002032 is the better-supported pick.

Both candidates are near-clones: same trait/phenotyping (Breast cancer; EFO breast carcinoma), same publication/date, same variant count (1,041,298), same training cohort and size (UKB; n=12,483), same ancestry distribution and validation size (n=48,968), and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC/R² shown, so not a strong differentiator). With endpoints/covariates identical (covariates=0) and full-model metrics/effect sizes essentially indistinguishable, the only visible edge is that PGS004040 (LDpred2.CV) has trivially higher full-model AUROC/R² and OR per SD than PGS004025 (LDpred2-auto). Given the tiny differences, this is a weak tie-break, hence low confidence.
